<!-- step:title="Why this matters" -->
Start from the practical problem. Explain why a student should care before
introducing vocabulary or equations.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Intuition" -->
Explain the concept in plain English. Use one idea per paragraph.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Building-block metaphor" viz="BuildingBlocksPKPD" -->
Use the course metaphor: dose as a box of blocks, PK as how blocks move through
the body, PD as what the final construction does, and variability as students
building differently.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Minimal math" -->
Show only the equation needed for the idea.

$$ y = f(x) $$

Then translate the equation back into words.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Worked example" -->
Use a concrete example. Warfarin is preferred when the concept fits the source
course material.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Common trap" -->
Name one frequent misunderstanding and explain how to avoid it.
<!-- /step -->

<!-- step:title="Key takeaways" -->
- One sentence students should remember.
- One modeling distinction they should not confuse.
- One practical implication.
<!-- /step -->
